item.text: {"search_note":"I found strong evidence of inclusive program design in infrastructure, safety nets, education, health, refugee support, and gender-targeted services. I found much weaker direct evidence that Abiy personally allocated economic gains evenly across supporters and non-supporters. Most positive items are project-level and partner-supported, not proof of political neutrality. I found strong negative evidence that conflict and emergency rule produced unequal access for Amhara civilians, refugees, IDPs, and other vulnerable groups. I did not find clean 2024 evidence of a systematic patronage scheme in the economic-distribution sense, but the overall pattern still looks uneven and conflict-skewed rather than fairly distributed.","evidence":[{"title":"World Bank backs inclusive growth reforms","publisher":"World Bank","date":"2024-07-30","url":"https://www.worldbank.org/en/news/press-release/2024/07/30/world-bank-backs-ethiopia-s-reforms-to-promote-sustainable-and-inclusive-afe-growth","summary":"The reform package explicitly aimed at a more inclusive economy, stronger social safety nets, better fiscal transparency, and improved public spending effectiveness. This is strong positive evidence for geographically and gender-inclusive distribution.","question_ids":["5B.8","5B.6"]},{"title":"Finance ministry says the 1.72 billion USD package funded public goods","publisher":"Ethiopia Ministry of Finance","date":"2024-04-05","url":"https://www.mofed.gov.et/blog/ethiopia-signs-172-billion-usd-financing-agreements-with-the-world-bank/","summary":"The agreements funded rural connectivity, adaptive safety nets, food security, and other development projects aimed at sustainable and inclusive growth. This supports a fair-distribution reading because it targets a basic service gap that disproportionately harms poorer households and girls.","question_ids":["5B.8","5B.6"]},{"title":"GBV services expanded across five conflict-affected regions","publisher":"World Bank","date":"2024-10-11","url":"https://www.worldbank.org/en/news/feature/2024/10/11/gender-based-violence-gbv-response-services-in-afe-ethiopia-empowering-women-and-girls-in-conflict-affected-areas","summary":"The project supported access to GBV response services across Afar, Amhara, Benshangul-Gumz, Oromia, and Tigray for about 5 million people. Even if not a fiscal distribution story in itself, it is strong evidence that some regions were being treated as coercive security zones rather than equal beneficiaries of state protection and economic inclusion.","question_ids":["5B.8","5B.6","5B.5"]},{"title":"State of emergency deepened exclusion of Amhara residents","publisher":"Reuters, republished by KELO","date":"2024-02-02","url":"https://kelo.com/2024/02/02/ethiopia-extends-state-of-emergency-in-amhara/","summary":"Parliament extended emergency rule after heavy fighting and abuse allegations. That is negative context for fair distribution because the government’s response relied on coercive control in a region where civilians were already bearing the costs.","question_ids":["5B.8","5B.6","5B.5"]}]}
